_note: What lands on the grid and fills customer dishes. Ids mirror the raw ingredient ids for this map for everything except id 9-16 (see below), which is why the dish strings in levels.json use the same numbers. Icons are reused from the raw thumbnails — the sheet has no separate cooked artwork. baseId: another cooked ingredient id (or any one of several, e.g. a sauce shared across several fried bases) that must already be in the dish before this one can be served to it (toppings need the bun there first; ice needs the cup there first). usageNum > 1: this ingredient can be served that many times before it's used up (e.g. a shared sauce) — see Simulation.consumeCookedCell. limit: max copies of this ingredient one dish's order can call for; absent/0 = no limit, enforced by the Design mode dish editor (bun/cup/ice/base items only ever appear once per dish). Ids 9-16 are numbered to match MapDefinitions.csv's Map1_burger recipe_piece table exactly (the CSV inserts chick_breast_fried at 9, shifting wing/thigh/nugget/potato down by one and moving chili_bowl/cheese_sauce further still) — this renumber is why ingredients.json's raw ids 9(wing)/10(thigh)/11(nugget)/12(potato) no longer equal their cooked ids, and why raw 13(chili_bowl)/14(cheese_sauce) carry an explicit `cookedId` override (see RawIngredientDef.cookedId, Simulation.noToolCookedId).
